messages:
noah_recruiting: Heads up 1: open enrollment question. Divorce finalized 2026-09-10. Im trying to remove my ex from my plans and switch spouse coverage to employee+child for my 2yo. OE opens 2026-10-01. Can I do this as a QLE now or wait for OE? Also worried about retro premiums for Sept paychecks.

devon_benefits: Sorry to hear that, @noah_recruiting. Divorce is a QLE. You can submit for a change effective date 2026-09-10 (date of decree). Since OE is coming, you can either process now as QLE or wait and make the change during OE; doing it now avoids overlap and double coverage. We'll need the divorce decree and completed QLE form.

noah_recruiting: If I submit now and it's effective 9/10, will OE overwrite that? I want employee+child to persist into next plan year.

devon_benefits: Good Q. If you process the QLE now and then during OE you re-confirm enrollments, the QLE effective change persists. OE enrollment is treated as election for the next plan year; carriers will keep dependent lines as you elect them during OE. Just ensure you select employee+child for the upcoming year as well.

karen_payroll: Payroll/proration: we prorate premiums to the event date. Example: if your pay period 9/16-9/30 included spouse premiums and event is 9/10, we remove spouse premiums starting 9/10 and calculate over/underpayment for that pay period. Overpaid spouse premiums get refunded via payroll credit or check once benefits confirms the QLE. Provide employee ID and QLE case number for speed.

noah_recruiting: Great. What about FSA or HSA contributions? Do I need to change elections mid-year?

devon_benefits: HSA eligibility could change if your plan tier changes (e.g., moving off a high-deductible plan). For FSA, dependent eligibility for dependent-care FSA depends on custody; removing a spouse doesn't automatically change your dependent care eligibility for your child. We'll review your FSA elections and advise if mid-year changes are allowed.

benefits-bot: Submit QLE here: https://benefits.redwood.com/qle  choose "Divorce/Legal separation" and attach decree. Deadline: 60 days from event. For OE: https://benefits.redwood.com/open-enroll

noah_recruiting: One more tricky bit: my ex is still on payroll for a contractor 1099 with Redwood until 9/25. Could that cause double coverage overlap if they are technically still associated in our HRIS?

ben_legal: Typically eligibility is tied to benefits enrollment records, not contractor association. If your ex remains on company-connected payroll briefly, that doesn't prevent removal from your benefits as spouse. However, keep documentation showing divorce date to avoid disputes. If carriers ask, we'll provide the decree.

karen_payroll: Also note if any premiums were paid to the other carrier because your ex added the child in their own plan, we can't retro-bill that carrier. We'll reconcile Redwood-side premiums and adjust your payroll only.

noah_recruiting: Sounds good. I'll upload the decree and file the QLE today. Can you open a case for me so I can track the refund?

devon_benefits: Case opened: DIV-2026-4410. Upload the decree to that case and fill desired effective date = 2026-09-10. We'll approve, notify payroll, and confirm OE continuity.

noah_recruiting: Thanks team 1 appreciate the speedy help. :pray:
